newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Supreme Court stays Uttar Pradesh ruling.
newsitem.headline: India's Supreme Court stays Uttar Pradesh ruling.

text.p: India's Supreme Court on Friday stayed a high court ruling which had ordered the lifting of direct federal rule in the nation's most populous state, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.
The agency said there would be a detailed hearing some time in January.
"This will not preclude the governor (of Uttar Pradesh) from exploring the possibility of formation of a popular government," the PTI quoted the three-judge bench of the Supreme Court as saying.

Court officials in Lucknow, capital of Uttar Pradesh state, said on Thursday that the Allahabad High Court upheld an appeal by leaders of the main opposition Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) against federal rule in the state.
The BJP on Thursday had demanded that Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda resign after the Allahabad high court ruling.
The federal government had appealed to the Supreme Court against the ruling of the Allahabad high court.

President Shankar Dayal Sharma, bowing to a decision by Deve Gowda's cabinet, in October imposed direct rule on the northern state after local elections resulted in a hung assembly and efforts to form a government failed.
The BJP, which emerged from the polls as the largest single party in the state legislature, had appealed to the Allahabad high court, arguing they had been denied a chance to form a government.

The BJP won 177 seats in the 425-member assembly, followed by Deve Gowda's United Front coalition with 134 seats. The lower-caste Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) won 67 seats and its ally, the Congress party, took 33 seats.

The assembly was suspended but not dissolved after the imposition of federal rule in the politically crucial state, which sends 85 lawmakers to the 545-member federal parliament, more than any other of India's 26 states.
The decision to impose federal rule over Uttar Pradesh, which has 140 million people, provoked an uproar from the BJP, which had expected an invitation to form a government.

The BJP briefly held power in the state beginning in 1991. But New Delhi dismissed its government after Hindu zealots demolished a 16th-century mosque in the Uttar Pradesh town of Ayodhya in December 1992.
